as_told.title: Errors in Epstein's Bannon interview about the Santa Fe Institute and quarks

plain: In a taped interview with the political strategist Steve Bannon, the financier Jeffrey Epstein gets many things wrong yet still sounds like a man who had been talking to people who knew what they were talking about, according to the mathematician Eric Weinstein, who has listened to it. Weinstein points to the errors: Epstein claims he founded the Santa Fe Institute, a research centre, around 1990 to 1993, when others founded it in 1984, and he garbles a point about quarks and the physicist Murray Gell-Mann. To Weinstein, the tape is a muddled echo of real insiders' knowledge.
